title: A well-ordered union of submodules with successive quotients of projective dimension at most n has projective dimension at most n
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n\ge0$ an integer and $M$ an $R$-module. Let $(E,\le)$ be a well-ordered set (a total order in which every nonempty subset has a least element) and $(M_e)_{e\in E}$ a family of $R$-submodules of $M$ such that $M_{e'}\subseteq M_e$ whenever $e'\le e$, and $M=\bigcup_{e\in E}M_e$. For $e\in E$ let $M_{<e}=\bigcup_{e'<e}M_{e'}$ (the union of a chain of submodules, hence a submodule of $M_e$; it is $0$ when $e$ is the least element of $E$). Assume that for every $e\in E$ the quotient module $M_e/M_{<e}$ has a projective resolution of length $\le n$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension], i.e. an exact sequence $0\to P_n\to\dots\to P_0\to M_e/M_{<e}\to0$ with every $P_i$ a projective $R$-module. Then $M$ has a projective resolution of length $\le n$.
